name: twisted-planter
why: The part ParCAD web opens first, so it has to build, and read right, on a stranger's first visit. Two bodies. The planter: a ruled star loft twisted 60° through nine sections, cut hollow by the same star inset 3 mm at the same section heights, with six drains set between the saucer's first ring of bumps. The saucer: a revolved dish with 37 domed bumps in rings of 1, 6, 12 and 18 (six more per ring keeps neighbours equally spaced), each the cap of a 4.4 mm sphere eased into the floor by smooth(2), the curvature-continuous blend, 37 closed stripes in one treatment and 2 s of the 3.3 s build; curvature_jump_per_mm is the largest step in curvature measured where any of them meets the floor or its dome, 1e-6 being the ceiling the reply rounds a round-off number up to. between_bodies reads the planter touching the bumps and nowhere else; 282 faces is the planter's 201 plus the dish's 7, one per dome and one per blend, so no bump was lost (see GOTCHAS.md, a union that drops solids). measure_wall_thickness reads the planter's wall at 2.0 mm with its rim edge rounded; on the sharp rim it reports hundredths of a millimetre at the edge itself, where the flared facet meets the flat top at an acute angle. The planter rests on the bumps over 0.000 mm² in 0 patches: `touching` here is a tangent point where a dome's top meets the planter's floor, not a seat, which is the distinction contact_mm2 exists to draw. Printed as drawn, up +z, the planter has no unsupported face at all and the saucer one, the dish underside over its bed patch; facet_sag_mm 0.1845 is how far this ruled loft's walls lie from the smooth loft through the same sections, which is the part's shape and not a mesh artefact.
